name: Al Rajhi Capital
legal_name: Al Rajhi Capital Company (a Saudi Closed Joint Stock Company)
founded: AR 2025: established 2008; website: operations commenced 18 Mar 2008. CMA licence 07068-37 dated 19 Jun 2007 (website); CR 1010241681 dated 1 Dhul Hijjah 1428H (11 Dec 2007) per FS note 1.
ownership_summary: Wholly owned subsidiary of Al Rajhi Banking and Investment Corporation (Al Rajhi Bank). Paid-up share capital SAR 500,000,000 plus statutory reserve SAR 250,000,000 (FS note 1 and 2025 statement of financial position). Chairman is the bank's chairman.

shareholders.holder: Al Rajhi Banking and Investment Corporation (Al Rajhi Bank)

government_link: No direct link found. Parent shareholders above 5% were not verified (see sa-alrajhi).
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of Al Rajhi Bank (sa-alrajhi), reported inside the bank's 'Investment services, brokerage and other' segment. Double counting: Al Rajhi Capital's balance sheet, income and AUM are consolidated in the bank; never add this record to sa-alrajhi. The segment (H1 2026 operating income SAR 1,121m) is close to but not identical with the standalone firm. The firm's own statements are standalone: it reports one subsidiary, Privileged Warehouses Company (Jebel Ali, UAE; holds a warehouse for its benefit), and its KSA investment properties are legally held by Al Rajhi Development Company, a fellow subsidiary of the bank. Fellow subsidiaries supply services: Ejada Systems (IT), Neoleap (professional services), ATMAAL (outsourced staff), Al Rajhi Takaful (insurance). Drahim (robo/PFM) is owned 67.48% by the bank, not by Al Rajhi Capital.

subsidiaries.name: Privileged Warehouses Company (UAE)
subsidiaries.activity: Holds the Jebel Ali Free Zone warehouse lease (investment property of SAR 217.8m) for the benefit of Al Rajhi Capital

footprint: Head office: 8467 King Fahad Road, Al Muruj District, Riyadh. About 16 offices (investment centres) across Saudi Arabia (website, 12 Oct 2026); no branch list rendered. Digital channels nationwide; international brokerage via 38 foreign markets. One UAE property vehicle.
customer_segments: Retail and affluent investors (app, funds, brokerage), families (Family Proposition), high-net-worth and institutional clients (discretionary portfolios, Wealth and Institutional Clients), corporates (investment banking, corporate finance, employee savings programme), endowments (73 awqaf entities), foreign and local institutions (securities lending, custody).
business_lines: Brokerage and securities services (Tadawul, Nomu, international, margin lending, securities lending and borrowing, custody); asset management (public funds, discretionary portfolios, private funds, REIT, ETF, real estate); wealth and institutional clients; investment banking (ECM, DCM, M&A, corporate finance and debt advisory, structured finance); research; proprietary investments. FY2025 income (SAR): brokerage 340.8m, asset management 716.3m, investment banking 180.3m, Murabaha special commission 334.8m, Sukuk 77.5m, dividends 285.7m, rental 104.4m, other operating 426.4m; total 2,465.2m.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Al Rajhi Capital is the wholly owned, fully Shariah-compliant CMA-licensed (07068-37) investment arm of Al Rajhi Bank. AUM was SAR 165.8bn at end-2025 (+35%), ranked #2 in KSA with a 13.3% share, and it is the #1 Saudi broker by value traded (15.5% in 2025) and in digital trading. FY2025 net profit was SAR 1,794m on operating income of SAR 2,465m, with asset management income of SAR 716m (+47%) and brokerage income of SAR 341m (-20%). One 'Alrajhi Capital' app combines Tadawul and international brokerage, mutual funds and a robo-advisory service (iOS rating 4.56 on 217,066 ratings), supported by about 38 international markets, single-stock options, securities lending and fully digital margin lending. The fund range is its own (about 40 funds listed, a new Tadawul-listed MSCI Saudi ETF in Aug 2026, a Fund Factory for private funds, 13+ private real estate funds). In June 2026 it announced a securities-finance technology partnership with EquiLend and a market-intelligence integration with Benzinga, and its 2026 priorities include international dealing, institutional trading, a client portal and alternatives. A Wealth and Institutional Clients division and discretionary portfolios for institutional and high-net-worth clients sit inside Al Rajhi Capital, while private banking sits in the bank.

private_banking.detail: Private banking is run by the parent bank (Private Banking segment; investment products 'offered through AlRajhi Capital', see sa-alrajhi). Al Rajhi Capital has a Wealth and Institutional Clients division (Head: Nawaf Alghemlas) and discretionary portfolios for institutional and high-net-worth clients; no eligibility thresholds published. AR 2025: the wealth division restructured, expanded its advisory capability and digital enablement, and took part (up to 40%) in advisory mandates.

asset_management.detail: AUM SAR 165.8bn (31 Dec 2025), #2 in KSA, 13.3% share. 40 funds listed on the website: local/regional/international equity, sukuk, savings and money market, multi-asset, awqaf (73 endowment entities served), real estate monthly distribution. 2025 Fund Factory launches: Indirect Financing Funds 2 and 3, Pharma Sukuk Fund, Private Conservative Fund and Monthly Distribution 3. Al Rajhi Awaeed (money market) AUM +163%. Al Rajhi REIT. New 'Al Rajhi MSCI Saudi Equity ETF' on Tadawul (code 9413, fee 0.25%, AUM SAR 94.4m on 12 Oct 2026; inception shown as 10-Aug-26). Funds are also listed on Tadawul Group's Edaa Connect platform.

brokerage.detail: #1 by value traded (15.5% in 2025; '13%+' on the 2Q26 deck) and #1 in margin-lending share and digital trading; Tadawul, Nomu and 38 international markets (website pages list GCC/MENA, US, UK and Hong Kong; homepage says 37+). International traded value +308% and revenue +200% in 2025. Channels: Alrajhi Capital Super App and Super Web, eTadawul web, Trader Lite with TradingView charts, phone trading centre and about 16 offices. 2025 additions: single-stock options, securities lending and borrowing (ISLA member), custody launch, fully digital margin lending (contracts +150%), voice-enabled orders. US stock discovery screens added in the Oct 2026 app update; Benzinga market-intelligence tools integrated for US equities (Jun 2026).

digital_investing.detail: 'AlRajhi Capital' app (iOS seller Al Rajhi Capital Company; v8.5.1 released 3 Oct 2026; first released 16 Mar 2023; 217,066 ratings, average 4.56): Tadawul and international brokerage, mutual funds, alerts, statements; Oct 2026 update adds US growth/dividend stock discovery and fund analytics (quarterly performance, top holdings, geographic allocation, risk analysis). Annual report: app integrates local and international brokerage, funds and a robo-advisory service; over 90% of client transactions are digital; new unified website in 2025. ARC Invest web portal (arcinvest.com.sa) for fund investors. Three app outage notices were posted in 2026 (31 Mar, 9 Apr, 28 Jun).

advisory.detail: CMA licence covers advising. Wealth and Institutional Clients division (relationship-based advisory); investment banking and corporate finance advisory; research covering 89 listed companies and 30+ macro reports in 2025; 140+ pre-IPO investor education sessions.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary Portfolio Management for institutional and high-net-worth clients: bespoke team per private portfolio, Investment Policy Statement, regular performance reports and a dedicated relationship manager. No minimum or fees published; AUM split not disclosed.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: AR 2025: robo-advisory (المستشار الآلي) portfolios and a corporate savings programme were updated in 2025 and are available in the app; the parent's report names the service 'alrajhi Mashora' (automated, algorithm-driven). A 'Robo Terms & Conditions' notice dated 19 Nov 2025 is in the newsroom. Portfolio construction, minimums, fees and any technology vendor were not found. Separate from Drahim, the bank's 67.48%-owned robo platform (see sa-alrajhi).

funds_platform.detail: Own funds distributed through investment centres, the app and ARC Invest; one fund listed on Edaa Connect (Tadawul Group). No third-party fund shelf found on the website. On its own balance sheet it holds SAR 612m (quoted) and SAR 242m (unquoted) of its own funds and SAR 27m and SAR 109m of other managers' funds.

structured_products.detail: No client structured products found on the website pages opened. The annual report mentions structured products only within the company's own proprietary portfolio (interest-rate risk section).

private_markets.detail: Real estate is a core line: managed real estate assets doubled in 2025; 13+ private real estate funds launched (combined size SAR 25.8bn+ per the parent report); a private fund above SAR 1bn exited at over 40% return on equity; Al Rajhi REIT (NAV per unit +5%); 10+ MoUs with government bodies, investors and developers. Fund Factory private funds (financing, sukuk, conservative). Proprietary investments team moved to active investments in 2025 and collaborated with large international fund managers to assess product fit and Shariah compliance. 2026 priority: expand alternatives and international public and private markets exposure.

islamic_wealth.detail: The company's stated objective is to provide Sharia-compliant financial products and services; it has a Sharia Board, purification of non-compliant income, Murabaha financing, sukuk, Mudaraba and awqaf (endowment) funds. IFN Investor 2025 'Best Fund House for Waqf Funds' and Euromoney 2025 'Best Sukuk House in Saudi Arabia' (per its annual report); the awards page lists Euromoney 'Sharia Fund Manager of the Year' for 2019 and 2021.

AR 2025 names Sulaiman Al Rajhi as Vice Chairman; the website lists him as a non-executive member chairing the Audit Committee.

open_items: No 30 Jun 2026 standalone statements or AUM: Al Rajhi Capital publishes annual statements only. Balance sheet and income are FY2025; the H1 2026 figures are the parent's segment (proxy).

Board (resolved 12 Oct 2026): the IFN Investor headline of 12 Jun 2026 refers to the Al Rajhi REIT Fund board (Rami AlKouz appointed 1 Jun 2026 after Saleh Alderaan's resignation on 26 Feb 2026, per Al Rajhi Capital circulars S29, S30). Company board appointment dates are still not published; no CMA/Tadawul filing applies to the unlisted subsidiary.

FS 2025 PDF is image-only and AR 2025 pages 39 onwards have no text layer; figures were read from page renders and a local macOS Vision OCR pass. Key numbers (total assets, income, profit, AUM) were also cross-checked against the AR key-figures table and the parent's report.

LinkedIn checks for the CEO, wealth, asset management, securities and digital heads returned no matching profiles; all marked 'Not verified'. CEO appointment date (26 Mar 2025) comes from a news report; CFO appointment (Feb 2026) from a search result whose page returned HTTP 403.

Robo-advisory ('alrajhi Mashora' per the parent's report): portfolio design, minimums, fees and any technology vendor not found; the Nov 2025 Robo T&C page contained no body text in the fetched content and its Arabic document was not opened.

'Global Trading Network' relationship is inferred from the international-brokerage login domain only; no announcement found. Execution brokers and custodians for international markets are not named by Al Rajhi Capital.

Client counts and headcount are not disclosed (only 'approximately 230 investment professionals' and growth rates). Investment-centre cities and the 16-office list were not available in the fetched pages.

Awards page lists no award after 2022; 2025 awards (Euromoney Best Broker in Saudi Arabia, Best Sukuk House; IFN Investor Best Waqf Fund House) come from the AR and the parent's report only. CMA register entry not checked directly; licence number from the firm's site and FS.

People pass X20 (12 Oct 2026): Saleh Al-Daraan marked Departed (CFO post now Imran Hameed; REIT board resignation 26 Feb 2026). Hani Al-Omari (Alamri) is 'Conflicting sources': in AR 2025 but absent from the website and his bio URL returns 404; no successor named. Abdullah Alghamedi (custody head) rests on the EquiLend release alone. Appointment dates are published only for Alkassem (Dec 2021) and Sikandar (Jun 2022), via the legacy management-team page (S31); none for AL-Hathloul, Alghemlas, Alkouz, Alodhaibi, Binrubaian, Nashar, Altowaim, Alzaid, Said or any board member.

Search-engine results also show a legacy bio page for a former Chief Digital Officer (Essam Almajid, ex Senior Director Retail Digital Channels at Al Rajhi Bank) and an undated, paywalled Zawya item on a 'Director of Investment Banking' (Mounir Chahine); the Almajid page returned no biography text when opened and neither item is recorded. CDO succession (Alibrahim → Alodhaibi) is not documented by the company.

LinkedIn: the search tool declines name-based look-ups, so no new profile verifications were possible; no profile URLs surfaced in role-based searches (a third-party post naming Alghemlas appeared without a profile link). Decision-makers remain 'Not verified'.
